title: Affirmative Resolution of Bourgain's Slicing Problem Using Guan's Bound
summary: Equation(56) has an extraneous square inside a time derivative; the following calculation is correct. Conditional on the stated Guan, geometric and entropy-stability inputs, the final matrix/entropy argument and Euclidean section implication pass the bounded checks.

problems.title: Spurious square inside the time derivative in equation(56)
problems.source_location: Acquired v1 PDF p15, equation(56), final term.
problems.claim: The final displayed chain-rule equality includes +(1-r)^(-3) d/dt E A_t^2.
hypotheses: The statement is used for an isotropic log-concave initial probability measure.
complete_check: The chain rule gives d(E Gamma_r)/dr=E Gamma_r/(1-r)+(1-r)^(-3) d(E A_t)/dt; the square inside the last derivative is extraneous.
For the standard Gaussian initial measure, A_t=(1+t)^(-1)I and Gamma_r=I. The derivative is0; the printed right-hand side is I/(1-r)-2I, equal to-2I/3 at r=1/4.
Deleting the superscript2 restores the correct equality, and d(E A_t)/dt=-E A_t² then yields the correct Lemma3.3(iv).
problems.calculation_type: Exact analytic chain rule and Gaussian specialization, checked by native auxiliary and separately checked by primary; no executable mathematical experiment.
problems.counterevidence: The next displayed line already uses the correct derivative identity and obtains the correct lemma. All later covariance and entropy inequalities use that correct version. No substantive defect in the checked main implication is established.
problems.repair: Delete the superscript2 in E A_t^2 inside the derivative in the final term of(56).
problems.repair_verification: The chain rule and the exact Gaussian specialization both verify this correction; later Lemma3.3(iv) matches.
problems.impact: Local printed identity is false as written, but the correct calculation is immediately supplied and no central theorem failure follows.
problems.severity_reason: A localized formula correction restores consistency without changing the main proof or hypotheses.

checked_non_problem_annotations.reasoning: The assigned DOI is10.1007/s00039-025-00718-w, but the actual acquired document is arXiv:2412.15044v1,19December2024,20pages. Isotropic probability measure means centered with covariance I. For a volume-one convex body, L_K=(det Cov(K))^(1/(2n)); for an isotropic log-concave measure, L_mu=exp(-Ent(mu)/m). Theorem1.1 asks for some affine hyperplane and its ordinary (n-1)-dimensional Euclidean section volume, not a central section in a specified direction.

The trace against (Gamma_1-Gamma_2)^2 is therefore at least epsilon||Gamma_1-Gamma_2||_HS^2/2. Independence gives E||Gamma_1-Gamma_2||_HS^2=2E||Gamma-E Gamma||_HS^2. Dividing by4(1-r) gives exactly epsilon/(4(1-r)) times the variance. For r>xi, take epsilon=xi; Lemma3.5 gives V=integral_xi^1 Var_HS(Gamma_r)/(1-r)dr<=8m/xi.
checked_non_problem_annotations.hypotheses: The tilted measures are full-dimensional, so their finite-time covariance matrices are positive definite; this makes the inverse well-defined. Positive-semidefinite trace order is sufficient.

checked_non_problem_annotations.reasoning: For R<1 set I_R=integral_xi^R q(r)dr. Lemma3.3(iii) gives q'=E||I-Gamma||_HS^2/(1-r)^2>=0. Exact finite-interval integration by parts gives integral_xi^R (1-r)q' dr=I_R-(1-xi)q(xi)+(1-R)q(R). The variance identity and C05 imply V_R>=a I_R-(1-xi)q(xi)+(1-R)q(R)>=a I_R-(1-xi)q(xi). Since V_R<=8m/xi, I_R is uniformly bounded; monotone convergence yields finite I=integral_xi^1 q. Monotonicity then yields0<=(1-R)q(R)<=integral_R^1 q->0, justifying the boundary-free equation(64).

checked_non_problem_annotations.scope: Explicit universal constant chain to L_n
checked_non_problem_annotations.result: checked symbolically by analytic reasoning; no numerical or software calculation
checked_non_problem_annotations.reasoning: Lemma3.1 gives q(xi)<=4m/(1-xi)^2. With a=xi/4, C06 yields I<= [32/xi^2+16/(xi(1-xi))]m. Because q is nondecreasing, integral_0^1 q<=I/(1-xi). Corollary3.2 gives D(mu||gamma_1)/m<=B, with B=16/[xi^2(1-xi)]+8/[xi(1-xi)^2]. Identity covariance gives L_mu=exp(D/m)/sqrt(2*pi*e)<=exp(B)/sqrt(2*pi*e). Using L_mu>=c_p L_n gives L_n<=c_p^-1 exp(B)/sqrt(2*pi*e) for n>=10. The finitely many smaller dimensions can be absorbed in the universal constant.

checked_non_problem_annotations.scope: Theorem1.2 to Theorem1.1 with Euclidean section units
checked_non_problem_annotations.result: checked by a direct elementary argument
checked_non_problem_annotations.reasoning: Let K have volume1 and let X be uniform on K, with positive-definite covariance Sigma. Choose a unit eigenvector u for its smallest eigenvalue sigma^2. Then sigma^2<= (det Sigma)^(1/n)=L_K^2. By coarea, the density g(s) of u dot X is exactly Vol_(n-1)(K intersect {u dot x=s}), since u is unit and Vol(K)=1. Chebyshev gives probability at least3/4 in an interval of length4sigma centered at E(u dot X), so some section has volume at least3/(16sigma)>=3/(16L_K). If all L_n<=C_*, choose c=3/(32C_*) to obtain the theorem's strict inequality >c. In dimension1, the nonempty point section has0-dimensional volume1.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterevidence_or_limit: No claim that Euclidean section area is invariant under arbitrary affine maps is needed. The hyperplane may be affine; no unsupported central-section or every-direction statement is introduced.

checked_non_problem_annotations.scope: Equation(56) local printed error and exact Gaussian check
checked_non_problem_annotations.result: localized repairable notation error; at most Minor, for primary adjudication
checked_non_problem_annotations.reasoning: Equation(56)'s last term is visibly printed +(1-r)^(-3) d/dt E A_t^2. Since Gamma_r=A_t/(1-r) and dt/dr=(1-r)^(-2), the chain rule instead gives +(1-r)^(-3) d/dt E A_t. For the standard Gaussian starting measure, A_t=(1+t)^(-1)I and Gamma_r=I. Thus the actual derivative is0. The printed RHS equals I/(1-r)-2I, which at r=1/4 is -2I/3. Replacing E A_t^2 by E A_t gives exact cancellation and the correct derivative.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterevidence_or_limit: The very next displayed line correctly substitutes d(E A_t)/dt=-E A_t^2 and proves the correct Lemma3.3(iv). The correction is deletion of the isolated superscript2 inside the derivative. The theorem, later matrix inequalities and entropy argument are unaffected; this is not a counterexample to slicing, Guan's bound or Lemma3.3(iv).
